claims.text: TC4 is an unmodified alpha + beta dual-phase Ti6Al4V alloy.
Untreated TC4 has low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions.
Low-temperature plasma nitriding of TC4 will create a nitrogen-enriched hardened surface layer.
Plasma nitriding can promote nitrogen diffusion without altering the beneficial substrate microstructure when temperature and time are controlled.
A temperature of 500–600 degrees Celsius or lower is typical for low-temperature plasma nitriding of titanium alloys.
Keeping the nitriding temperature sufficiently low will avoid extensive alpha-case formation.
The treatment will form a thin, diffusion-hardened, nitrogen-enriched surface layer that transitions gradually to the unmodified bulk.
The nitrogen-enriched layer will contain TiN and/or nitrogen-strengthened alpha-Ti.
Nitrogen incorporation forms hard nitride phases and/or produces solid-solution strengthening of the alpha phase.
The hardened surface layer increases resistance to plastic deformation and wear.
A gradient microstructure minimizes adverse effects on substrate toughness and fatigue resistance.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will have significantly greater surface hardness than untreated TC4.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will have a lower wear rate than untreated TC4.
The ductility and high specific strength of the TC4 core will be largely maintained because nitriding has a limited penetration depth.
The proposed improvement applies primarily where surface-initiated damage, such as sliding wear or contact fatigue, is critical.
The modified layer is expected to remain beneficial only within an operating-temperature range that does not induce further phase transformations or oxidation.
An overly thick or brittle hardened layer could compromise fatigue properties.
